title: The GenAI system map
summary: A GenAI product is a stack of decisions, from the model call to knowledge, tools, agents, proof and operations. Each chapter owns some of those decisions.
useIf: You need to place a problem on the stack before you pick a technology.
avoidIf: You already know which layer is failing and need the details of that layer.

explain.md: A user question travels through layers. First the **model call** fixes the token budget, the controls and the API style (w01), and the **latency and caching** layer decides what is affordable (w02). **Knowledge** layers get the right content to the model: ingestion, chunking and indexes, retrieval, guardrails and access control (w03 to w07). **Tools and protocols** let the model act and talk to other systems (w08 MCP, w09 A2A). **Agents** coordinate several steps (w10 patterns, w11 Microsoft Agent Framework, w12 Foundry hosted agents and Agent 365).

explain.title: One question, nine stops
explain.alt: A question passes through model and API, latency and cache, knowledge, tools and protocols and agents to an answer, which is then checked by senses, proof and operations chapters.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  Q[Question] --> B[Budget and API w01]
  B --> L[Latency and cache w02]
  L --> K[Knowledge w03 to w07]
  K --> T[Tools and protocols w08 w09]
  T --> A[Agents w10 to w12]
  A --> R[Answer]
  R --> S[Senses w13]
  R --> P[Proof w14 w15]
  R --> O[Operate w16 w17]

explain.md: After the answer exists, three more concerns apply to every layer: **senses** (images and audio, w13), **proof** (evaluation and observability, w14 and w15) and **operations** (cost, reliability, governance, w16 and w17). Field notes (w18) and boss rounds (w19) combine them.

explain.caption: Which chapter owns the decision
head: Symptom
Likely layer
Chapter
rows: Parameter rejected, output cut off, wrong API
First token is slow, bill too high from repeated prompts
Answer is missing from the system, or chunks are cut badly
Right chunk exists but is not retrieved
Model answers anyway, or leaks another user's data
Nobody can show it works or why it broke

explain.title: Start with the least machinery
explain.md: Anthropic's guide to building agents advises finding the simplest solution possible, because agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance [[tr1]]. Climb the stack only when an eval shows the lower layer fails.

whereToUse: Triage: a complaint arrives and you must decide who owns the investigation
Design reviews: check that every layer has an owner and a metric
Interviews: say where on the stack a problem lives before you name a technology
Planning study: pick the chapters that match your role
Onboarding: give new engineers one picture of how the pieces connect

use: A failure has several plausible causes in different layers
A proposal adds a layer such as an agent and nobody has shown the lower layers fall short
You must explain a system to non-specialists
avoid: You are tuning one known parameter: go straight to that topic
You treat the map as a mandatory pipeline: many products need only two or three layers
The failing layer is already known and instrumented: go straight to that layer's topic
flips: The corpus fits the context window and has one tenant: drop the knowledge layers and use the prompt
Steps vary at run time and need tools: add tools before you add agents
Regulation or per-user data is involved: access control and governance move from last to first

pitfalls.symptom: A team adds RAG to fix a style problem
pitfalls.cause: The failing layer was not identified before choosing a fix
pitfalls.fix: Name the symptom, find the layer in the map, then choose the cheapest fix at that layer

pitfalls.symptom: An agent is built for a task a workflow could do
pitfalls.cause: Complexity was chosen before simpler layers were tested
pitfalls.fix: Start with a prompt, add retrieval or tools only when evals show a gap

pitfalls.cause: Access control sits in the knowledge layers, not in the model call
pitfalls.fix: Decide the permission model at ingestion, when ACLs are captured, not after launch

scenarios.title: The policy answer is out of date
scenarios.situation: Users report that the assistant quotes an old policy. The document was updated yesterday. A trace shows the retrieval step returned the old chunk.
constraints: The assistant answers from a search index
The index returned the previous version of the text
unknowns: How does new content reach the index?
Are old chunks deleted when a document changes?
scenarios.question: Where do you investigate first?

options.name: Switch to a larger model
options.why: The model faithfully used the old chunk. A larger model cannot fix missing fresh data.
options.tradeoff: A larger model helps when the right chunk is present but the model misreads it.

options.name: The ingestion and update path (w03)
options.why: The index holds old text, so the update or delete path failed before retrieval or the model were involved.
options.tradeoff: You must instrument sync lag and deletes to see the cause.

options.name: Response and semantic caches (w02)
options.why: A cache can also serve a stale answer, so rule it out second.
options.tradeoff: The trace already shows old retrieval output, so this is less likely the root cause.

flips.if: The trace shows the new chunk was retrieved but the answer is old
flips.then: Look at caches (w02) and then prompt assembly.
Fix deletes and versioning in ingestion, and add a freshness filter.

scenarios.takeaway: Locate the layer with the trace, then fix at that layer.

scenarios.title: How much machinery for a small knowledge base
scenarios.situation: A team plans a multi-agent assistant for 40 stable internal pages (about 60,000 tokens) used by one department. Risk is low and budget is small.
constraints: Corpus is small and rarely changes
unknowns: What accuracy does a baseline reach on a golden set?
scenarios.question: What architecture do you propose first?

options.name: RAG with hybrid search and a reranker
options.why: Works and scales when the corpus grows.
options.tradeoff: Adds ingestion, an index and retrieval tuning that the constraints do not need.

options.name: Multi-agent system with a retrieval agent and a writer agent
options.why: It adds coordination cost and failure modes for a problem one call can solve.
options.tradeoff: Multi-agent fits independent subtasks with large, separate contexts.

options.name: Single prompt with the pages, plus prompt caching
options.why: The corpus fits the window, changes rarely and has one audience, so the simplest layer meets every constraint.
options.tradeoff: It stops scaling if the corpus grows past a comfortable window or permissions appear.

flips.if: The corpus grows past what fits in the window or accuracy drops deep in context
flips.then: Move to RAG and measure retrieval quality.

flips.if: Different users may see different pages
flips.then: Choose retrieval with per-user access control.

scenarios.takeaway: Climb the stack only when a measured gap forces it.

quiz.q: Match each symptom to the chapter that owns it.

pairs.l: A parameter is rejected with HTTP 400
First token arrives after many seconds
Relevant chunk exists but is never returned
A user sees another team's document

quiz.explain: Parameter rules belong to the model call chapter, slow first tokens to latency and caching, missed chunks to retrieval and leaks across users to access control.

quiz.q: A task fits comfortably in the context window and the facts rarely change. What does the system map suggest first?
options: A single prompt, adding layers only if evals fail
quiz.explain: Use the least machinery that meets the constraints. Agents, fine-tuning and vector stores each add cost that the stated dials do not justify.

quiz.q: Which concerns apply across every layer of the stack?
quiz.explain: Proof, operations and governance apply to all layers. Temperature is a single model-call control in w01.

flashcards.front: Name the nine stops a question passes through.
flashcards.back: Budget and API, latency and cache, knowledge, tools and protocols, agents, then senses, proof and operations around the answer.

flashcards.front: What is the default rule for how much of the stack to use?
flashcards.back: Use the simplest layer that meets the constraints, and add retrieval, tools or agents only when a measured gap appears.

flashcards.front: Where does access control get decided?
flashcards.back: At ingestion, when ACLs are captured, and at query time through filters. It is not a late add-on.
